directAnswer: Charging an EV from a normal socket typically provides about 3-5 miles of range per hour of charging, depending on the vehicle and socket type.
summary: Charging an electric vehicle (EV) from a standard household outlet is a slower process compared to dedicated EV chargers, impacting the total range added per hour.

sections.heading: Charging Speed from a Normal Socket
sections.body: A normal 120V outlet can charge an EV at a rate of approximately 1.2 kW, resulting in 3-5 miles of range per hour. This is significantly slower than Level 2 chargers, which can provide 10-60 miles of range per hour.

sections.heading: Factors Affecting Range
sections.body: The actual range added depends on several factors including the EV model, battery capacity, and the efficiency of the vehicle. Additionally, environmental factors such as temperature can influence charging efficiency.

sections.heading: Charging Time Estimates
sections.body: For a typical EV with a 60 kWh battery, charging from a normal socket can take over 24 hours to fully charge from empty, making it impractical for daily use unless the vehicle is parked for extended periods.

steps.title: Identify Your EV's Charging Needs
steps.detail: Check your EV's manual or manufacturer's website to determine the battery capacity and charging specifications.

steps.title: Assess Your Home's Electrical System
steps.detail: Ensure your home's electrical system can support the charging needs of your EV without overloading circuits.

steps.title: Connect the EV to the Socket
steps.detail: Use the appropriate charging cable to connect your EV to the standard outlet, ensuring a secure fit.

steps.title: Monitor Charging Progress
steps.detail: Keep track of the charging progress through your vehicle's dashboard or mobile app, if available.

faqs.question: Can I charge my EV overnight using a normal socket?
faqs.answer: Yes, charging overnight is common, but ensure your EV has enough time to charge fully based on your daily driving needs.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Level 1 and Level 2 charging?
faqs.answer: Level 1 charging uses a standard 120V outlet, while Level 2 charging uses a 240V outlet, providing faster charging times.

faqs.question: Is it safe to charge my EV from a normal socket?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the outlet is in good condition and the electrical system is capable of handling the load, it is safe to charge from a normal socket.

caveats: Charging times can vary based on the specific EV model and battery size.
Not all normal sockets are suitable for EV charging; consult an electrician if unsure.
